# SEO-113: Serve a sitemap that conforms to the sitemap protocol schema

This page is generated from the canonical JSONL registry record. Edit the JSONL record and run `npm run docs -- --write`; do not edit this file directly.

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Domain | `sitemaps` |
| Category | `TECHNICAL_SEO` |
| Minimum level | `LITE` |
| Severity | `HIGH` |
| Impact | `HIGH` |
| Change safety | `REVIEW_REQUIRED` |
| Evidence tier | `A` |
| Confidence | `HIGH` |

## Statement

Every published sitemap and sitemap index parses as XML, uses the protocol namespace, contains only the elements the protocol defines, and gives each entry a fully qualified URL rather than a path.

## Rationale

A file that fails to parse or uses an unrecognised namespace is rejected whole rather than partially, so a single malformed entry can discard the entire submission without any visible symptom on the site.

## Applicability

```json
{
  "all": [
    "public_site"
  ],
  "any": [
    "has_sitemap"
  ]
}
```

## Implementation

Generate the file from the route inventory rather than maintaining it by hand, escaping URL entities as the protocol requires. Validate the generated output against the schema as part of the build so a malformed entry fails before it is published.

## Verification

- Level: `SOURCE_AND_RUNTIME`
- Method: Fetch each published sitemap URL and parse the body against the protocol schema, recording the namespace, element names, and any parse failure.
- Evidence: `SITEMAP`, `VALIDATOR_OUTPUT`, `HTTP_STATUS`
- Automated check: `sitemap-xml-wellformed`

## Scope

- Search surfaces: `GOOGLE_SEARCH`, `BING_SEARCH`
- Frameworks: `any`
- Caution: This control governs the sitemap a site publishes. Publishing one is not treated as mandatory here, because the documented guidance describes it as helpful for large or poorly linked sites rather than as a universal requirement.
